name: conflict-scope-definition
claim: Two active prescriptions share conflict scope when they occupy overlapping territory along at least one axis (tag, subject ref, subject type) within the same domain - overlap signals the pair is close enough that a contradiction would be meaningful. Contradictory prescriptions are actionable conflicts; contradictory inferences are dissent and live outside this audit's scope.

rules.then: They overlap only if they are in the same domain or both have no domain; distinct non-nil domains never overlap

rules.given: Two active prescriptions in the same domain
rules.then: They overlap if they share a tag, share a subject ref, share a subject type, or both carry empty tags and subjects (domain-global)

rules.given: A pair flagged by the audit
rules.then: The audit surfaces the candidate pair; whether the pair actually contradicts, is redundant, or is compatible requires reviewer judgment

invariants: Overlap is symmetric - overlap(a,b) iff overlap(b,a)
A node does not overlap with itself
Cross-domain pairs with distinct non-nil domains never overlap
Overlap is a necessary but not sufficient condition for contradiction
The audit surfaces candidates; resolution requires reviewer judgment

evidence.detail: Accepted via human adjudication against cb:b032. Reasoning: cb-schema-v2: conflict scope re-attaches to active directives - the audit is response-to-violation machinery and a theory cannot be violated. Inference-conflict (structured dissent) is consensus-thread work, explicitly out of scope.

Retro-pair per the b507 close protocol: the session slug this node stipulates from is readable in the thread record - the schema-landing main body and postscripts 2-6 cover the stasis, observability, and ceremony exchanges where these stipulations were made.
